evals.prompt: Design a parameterised synchronous FIFO in SystemVerilog for our block: configurable data width and depth (depth must be a power of two), full and empty flags, and a registered read (no first-word fall-through). Put it in fifo_sync.sv.
evals.expected_output: fifo_sync.sv: one module, ANSI ports with comments, power-of-two depth check, _q/_d registers, async active-low reset on control only; passes svstyle check, Verilator -Wall and Yosys synth.

evals.prompt: I need a SystemVerilog state machine that talks to a slow slave over a req/ack handshake: raise req when start_i pulses, wait for ack, drop req. The slave can take up to 16 cycles to answer, so add a timeout that aborts the transfer and sets a sticky error flag until clear_i. Registered outputs please.
evals.expected_output: An enum-typed FSM (package + module or module alone), state_q/state_d, unique case with default, commented case arms, registered outputs, timeout counter; passes svstyle check, Verilator -Wall and Yosys synth.

evals.prompt: write me a 2-flop synchronizer module and a toggle-based pulse synchronizer that uses it, to move single-cycle pulses from a fast clock domain to a slow one. sv please, each module in its own file
evals.expected_output: Two files (sync_2ff-like and pulse sync), toggle in source domain registered before crossing, two flops in destination, edge detect; passes svstyle check, Verilator -Wall and Yosys synth.

evals.prompt: Can you code a round-robin arbiter in SystemVerilog? N requesters as a parameter (default 4), one-hot grant, the grant is registered and lasts one cycle, and priority rotates past the last winner.
evals.expected_output: rr_arbiter-like module, parameterised N with check, one-hot registered grant, rotating priority; passes svstyle check, Verilator -Wall and Yosys synth.

evals.prompt: Here's an old Verilog UART transmitter, evals/files/uart_tx.v. Bring it up to our SystemVerilog house style as uart_tx.sv, keeping its behaviour identical cycle for cycle. Rename the ports clk->clk_i, rst_n->rst_ni, start->start_i, data->data_i, tx->tx_o, busy->busy_o and the parameter CLKS_PER_BIT->ClksPerBit; everything else is up to you.
evals.expected_output: uart_tx.sv: ANSI ports, logic, always_ff, begin/end, commented; passes svstyle check, Verilator -Wall and Yosys; simulates identically to the original.

checks.text: Simulates cycle-for-cycle identically to the original

evals.prompt: This block tapes out next week. Review evals/files/pkt_stats.sv and fix everything that is wrong with it; keep the port list.
evals.expected_output: pkt_stats.sv with the latch on err_o removed, the 16-to-8-bit truncation of count_o resolved, and the 4-bit level no longer crossing clock domains bit by bit (Gray code or handshake).

checks.text: The multi-bit level crossing uses Gray code or a handshake (CDC-002)

evals.prompt: Write an asynchronous FIFO in SystemVerilog: parameterised data width and power-of-two depth, separate write and read clocks and resets, full and empty flags. Put it in async_fifo.sv (submodules in their own files if you use any).
evals.expected_output: Gray-coded pointers crossed through two-flop synchronisers, full/empty computed from the synchronised Gray pointers, depth check; passes svstyle check --synth, Verilator -Wall and Yosys.

checks.text: Pointers cross the clock domains in Gray code (CDC-003)

evals.prompt: I need a ready/valid skid buffer in SystemVerilog that sustains full throughput and cuts the combinational path from the downstream ready back to the upstream ready. skid_buffer.sv, parameterised data width.
evals.expected_output: Two-entry skid buffer; upstream ready registered; handshake signal names state the protocol (PRT-007); passes svstyle check --synth, Verilator -Wall and Yosys.

checks.text: Handshake names state the protocol, e.g. _ready_and_o (PRT-007)

evals.prompt: Write a single-port synchronous RAM in SystemVerilog, 256 words of 32 bits with per-byte write enables, written so that FPGA and ASIC synthesis infer a memory rather than a bank of flops. ram_sp.sv.
evals.expected_output: Unreset memory array written in always_ff with byte enables, registered read; Yosys infers a memory; passes svstyle check --synth and Verilator -Wall.

checks.text: Yosys infers a memory, not flops

evals.prompt: Our integration harness instantiates TopModule with exactly these ports: input clk, input reset (synchronous, active-high), input [7:0] in, output [7:0] out. For each bit, out[i] must be 1 in the cycle after in[i] was sampled changing from 0 to 1, and 0 otherwise. Reset clears out and the remembered previous input to 0. Write it in SystemVerilog, TopModule.sv.
evals.expected_output: TopModule.sv with the given module and port names and a synchronous active-high reset, house style inside (comments, _q flops), NAM-002/RST-001 waived with a reason; passes svstyle check --synth and the edge-detect testbench.

checks.text: The given ports are kept exactly: clk, reset, in, out
Matches the reference behaviour cycle for cycle

evals.prompt: Review evals/files/pkt_stats.sv before it goes to the design review. Do not change it; write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: review.md naming the latch on err_o, the 16-to-8-bit truncation of count_o, and the 4-bit level crossing clock domains with a synchroniser per bit (CDC-002); pkt_stats.sv left untouched.

checks.text: Finds the truncation of the 16-bit count to count_o
Finds the per-bit synchronisation of level (CDC-002)

evals.prompt: Can you review evals/files/review_ok/sat_counter.sv? Do not change it; write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: review.md that reports the block as correct with no rule violations: one clock, so no CDC or reset-synchroniser findings; sat_counter.sv left untouched.

checks.text: No clock-domain or reset-synchroniser finding on a one-clock block

evals.prompt: Please review evals/files/review_subtle/level_monitor.sv before tape-out. Do not change it; write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: review.md naming the four bugs that lint and svstyle miss: corrected_q holds a two's-complement value but is unsigned, so the magnitude compare is wrong (LNG-018); the one-cycle over_q pulse crosses from 200 MHz to 25 MHz through a two-flop synchroniser and is lost (CDC-005); active is combinational logic driving a crossing (CDC-004); the pad reset is used raw in both domains with no reset synchroniser (RST-002/RST-003). level_monitor.sv left untouched.

checks.text: Finds the one-cycle pulse lost crossing to the slower clock (CDC-005)
Finds combinational logic driving a crossing (CDC-004)
Finds the pad reset released without a synchroniser (RST-002/RST-003)
